name: r7-m12
statement: Three RL-written solved examples in context raise the cued base only on test problems that share a subject with an example, because the base copies that subject's routine (its setup and the check that closes it) and gains no new capability, so a draw's gain equals the base's fixable errors (problems it solves in some samples but not all) in the subjects the draw covers.
scope: Covers allenai/Olmo-3-1025-7B with the three-token cue on MATH-500 at T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, grader v3, with three solved examples written by Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math placed before the prompt (shots1 / shots1b). Does not cover: hard328 (competition problems share few MATH-500 subject routines, so no gain is expected there), T 0.6 cells where loops dominate, the RL model itself, weight edits, or examples written by the base, which carry no routine the base lacks. The cap-hit rise under long examples is outside the mechanism. Conflicts were looked for and are listed.

explains.how: The two RL-written draws use different example problems and so cover different subjects; draw 1 (problems 0-2: Precalculus, Intermediate Algebra, Algebra) covers the subjects that hold most of the base's fixable errors.
The base's errors are concentrated in Intermediate Algebra, one of draw 1's subjects, so a draw covering it has the most fixable errors in reach.
Base-written examples of the same three problems cover the same subjects but carry the base's own routine, so the base has nothing new to copy.
Competition problems rarely match a MATH-500 subject routine, so subject-confined copying predicts no gain on hard328.

explains.quote: missed: the RL-shots gain did not repeat
explains.how: A second draw on other subjects reaches fewer fixable errors, so a forecast that treats the gain as a property of RL-written text, whatever the subjects, fails.

conflicts.quote: Rasch + one bilinear term gains nothing held out
conflicts.how: A subject-confined gain is a second, subject-specific axis, but the one-axis fit over 36 arms (the examples arms included) finds none; the test's stated power (about 1.8 problems for a planted axis) leaves room, but it does not support the mechanism.

Code-RL is also an RL writer whose math answers differ from the base's, yet its examples of the same subjects give no gain; the mechanism has to say Code-RL's texts lack the Math-RL check, and that is not shown.
On hard328 the examples lengthen answers and add cap hits across the board: a global effect of the examples' register that subject confinement does not predict.

conflicts.quote: RL's examples are longer (8,240 vs 4,853 tokens)
conflicts.how: The examples arm differs from the base-written arm in length and cap hits, which points to a global length/register channel that competes with the subject channel.

rival: The strongest rival is register transfer. Under it, RL-written examples move the cued base toward RL's longer, check-heavy register in every subject. A draw's gain then depends on properties of its texts (length, how often they check), and the gain spreads over subjects in proportion to the base's errors. The two are separated by where draw 1's gain falls. The rival puts about 60 % of draw 1's net gain in the matched subjects, because those subjects hold that share of base errors, which gives a matched-minus-unmatched per-problem contrast near 0.015. This mechanism puts nearly all of it there, a contrast near 0.08.

predictions.experiment: Mechanism test: per-problem gain of the RL-written-examples arm (draw 1) over the mean of the 4 cued-base samples, averaged over problems in the subjects of example problems 0-2, minus the same average over all other subjects. The register-transfer rival (gain spread in proportion to base errors) predicts about 0.015; subject confinement predicts about 0.08.
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json with its manifest.json, and studies/rlneurons/results/rln4/t1_t2_items-01/per_problem.json. Arm R = the vectors.json arm whose manifest entry is the cued base with 3 solved examples written by Math-RL (Olmo-3.1-7B-RL-Zero-Math) of MATH-500 problems 0, 1, 2 (shots1, draw 1). Arms B0-B3 = base_cue_s0, base_cue_s1, base_cue_s2, base_cue_s3. Align every arm to problem_index through vectors.json problem_indices. Drop problem_index 0, 1 and 2, and any problem whose entry in R or in any B arm is null or missing. Per problem b = (B0+B1+B2+B3)/4 and g = R - b; vector entries are v3 0/1, and cap hits are already 0. M = the set of per_problem.json subject values of problem_index 0, 1 and 2. Statistic S = mean of g over the kept problems whose per_problem.json subject is in M, minus mean of g over the kept problems whose subject is not in M. Problems absent from per_problem.json are dropped.

predictions.experiment: Case where the effect should not appear: the same matched-minus-unmatched contrast for the base-written-examples arm, which uses the same three example problems and so the same subjects. The examples carry the base's own routine, so the mechanism predicts no subject contrast.
predictions.recipe: Files as in the first recipe. Arm E = the vectors.json arm whose manifest job id is abaybektursun-1114-183855-e840 (cued base with 3 base-written examples). Arms B0-B3 = base_cue_s0 to base_cue_s3. Drop problem_index 0, 1, 2 and any problem whose entry in E or in any B arm is null or missing. Per problem g = E - (B0+B1+B2+B3)/4. M = subjects of problem_index 0, 1, 2 in per_problem.json. Statistic S_E = mean g over kept problems with subject in M minus mean g over kept problems with subject not in M. Problems absent from per_problem.json are dropped.

predictions.experiment: Cause: the examples only let the base copy a routine on problems it can already solve. On problems the cued base solved in 0 of its 4 samples, the RL-written-examples arm should do no better than a fresh base sample (about 5 right). A rival in which the examples pass on RL's capability predicts about RL's single-sample rate there, about 9 to 10.
predictions.recipe: Files: studies/rlneurons/results/axis/math500-01/vectors.json with manifest.json. Arm R as in the first recipe (Math-RL-written examples of problems 0-2, draw 1); B0-B3 = base_cue_s0 to base_cue_s3. Drop problem_index 0, 1, 2 and any problem whose entry in R or in any B arm is null or missing. Z = kept problems with B0+B1+B2+B3 == 0. Statistic = number of problems in Z where R == 1 (an integer; cap hits are already 0 in the vectors). Also report |Z|.

predictions.experiment: New draw on the other subjects. Build 3 RL-written examples, one each from Number Theory, Counting & Probability and Geometry: for each subject, the stored T2 text (s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl, RL plain, T 1.0) of the lowest problem_index in that subject (subject from per_problem.json) with t2_right true, t2_cap_hit false and t2_generated_tokens <= 6000. Place them before the prompt in the shots1 format (run_cell --shots), then the prompt with the cue. Run the base on every MATH-500 problem of those three subjects except the 3 example problems (about 138), T 1.0 / top-p 1.0, cap 16,384, 1 sample, run_cell's default seeds, grader v3, cap hits wrong.
predictions.unit: right of the ~138 Number Theory, Counting & Probability and Geometry test problems
predictions.refuted_by: fewer than 118 right, or a gain under +2 problems over the mean of base_cue_s0-s3 (axis vectors.json) on the same problems

intervention.change: Before each test prompt, place 3 solved examples from the test problem's own subject, written by Math-RL. For each of the 7 subjects, the examples are the stored RL T2 answers (s3 r4/modal_t2-01/t2/T2.jsonl) of the 3 lowest-problem_index problems in that subject with t2_right true, t2_cap_hit false and t2_generated_tokens <= 4000; a test problem that is one of its subject's examples is replaced by that subject's next qualifying problem. The format is shots1's (run_cell --shots), and the opening cue still follows the prompt. Everything else is the usual cell.

cell.prompt: 3 same-subject Math-RL-written solved examples, then the standard prompt, then the prefilled three-token opening cue
cell.seeds: run_cell default per-request seeds (as in the shots1 cells)

intervention.count: right answers over all 500 MATH-500 problems by grader v3; cap hits and empty answers count wrong

best_known.setting: base + cue, T 1.0, vote over 4 samples after restart, ties to the shortest finished sample (19,697 tokens per problem)

intervention.why: If a draw's gain is the base's fixable errors in the subjects its examples cover, then matching the examples' subject to every test problem extends draw 1's matched-subject gain to all 500 problems, against 410 for the cued base alone.
